128006.subject: Zoology
128006.text: Which of the following is a reason why frogs are beneficial to agriculture?
options: They eat insects that damage crops
They attract birds that protect crops
128006.sol: Frogs have well organised male and female reproductive systems. Male reproductive organs consist of a pair of yellowish ovoid testes , which are found adhered to the upper part of kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum called mesorchium. Vasa efferentia are 10-12 in number that arise from testes. They enter the kidneys on their side and open into Bidder’s canal. Finally it communicates with the urinogenital duct that comes out of the kidneys and opens into the cloaca. The cloaca is a small, median chamber that is used to pass faecal matter, urine and sperms to the exterior. The female reproductive organs include a pair of ovaries The ovaries are situated near kidneys and there is no functional connection with kidneys. A pair of oviduct arising from the ovaries opens into the cloaca separately. A mature female can lay 2500 to 3000 ova at a time. Fertilisation is external and takes place in water. Development involves a larval stage called tadpole. Tadpole undergoes metamorphosis to form the adult.Frogs are beneficial for mankind because they eat insects and protect the crop. Frogs maintain ecological balance because these serve as an important link of food chain and food web in the ecosystem. In some countries the muscular legs of frog are used as food by man.

129484.subject: Zoology
129484.text: What are nephrons in the kidney?
129484.sol: Each kidney has nearly one million complex tubular structures called nephrons (Figure 16.3), which are the functional units. Each nephron has two parts – the glomerulus and the renal tubule. Glomerulus is a tuft of capillaries formed by the afferent arteriole – a fine branch of renal artery. Blood from the glomerulus is carried away by an efferent arteriole. The renal tubule begins with a double walled cup-like structure called Bowman’s capsule, which encloses the glomerulus. Glomerulus alongwith Bowman’s capsule, is called the malpighian body or renal corpuscle (Figure 16.4). The tubule continues further to form a highly coiled network – proximal convoluted tubule. (PCT). A hairpin shaped Henle’s loop is the next part of the tubule which has a descending and an ascending limb. The ascending limb continues as another highly coiled tubular region called distal convoluted tubule (DCT). The DCTs of many nephrons open into a straight tube called collecting duct, many of which converge and open into the renal pelvis through medullary pyramids in the calyces.

130893.subject: Zoology
130893.text: How many sperms are released during a coitus?
130893.sol: It is a microscopic structure composed of a head, neck, a middle piece and a tail. A plasma membrane envelops the whole body of sperm. The sperm head contains an elongated haploid nucleus, the anterior portion of which is covered by a cap-like structure, acrosome. The acrosome is filled with enzymes that help fertilisation of the ovum. The middle piece possesses numerous mitochondria, which produce energy for the movement of tail that facilitate sperm motility essential for fertilisation. The human male ejaculates about 200 to 300 million sperms during a coitus of which, for normal fertility, at least 60 per cent sperms must have normal shape and size and at least 40 per cent of them must show vigorous motility.

132201.subject: Zoology
132201.text: According to Morgan's findings, what was the proportion of parental gene combinations compared to non-parental types when genes were on the same chromosome?
options: Parental gene combinations were much higher
132201.sol: Morgan and his group knew that the genes were located on the X chromosome (Section 4.4) and saw quickly that when the two genes in a dihybrid cross were situated on the same chromosome, the proportion of parental gene combinations were much higher than the non-parental type. Morgan attributed this due to the physical association or linkage of the two genes and coined the term linkage to describe this physical association of genes on a chromosome and the term recombination to describe the generation of non-parental gene combinations (Figure 4.11). Morgan and his group also found that even when genes were grouped on the same chromosome, some genes were very tightly linked (showed very low recombination) (Figure 4.11, Cross A) while others were loosely linked (showed higher recombination) (Figure 4.11, Cross B). For example he found that the genes white and yellow were very tightly linked and showed only 1.3 per cent recombination while white and miniature wings showed 37.2 percent recombination. His student Alfred Sturtevant used the frequency of recombination between gene pairs on the same chromosome as a measure of the distance between genes and ‘mapped’ their position on the chromosome.

132221.subject: Zoology
132221.text: In the XO type of sex determination, what is the sex of fertilized eggs with sperms having an X-chromosome?
132221.sol: It was also observed that in a large number of insects the mechanism of sex determination is of the XO type, i.e., all eggs bear an additional X-chromosome besides the other chromosomes (autosomes). On the other hand, some of the sperms bear the X-chromosome whereas some do not. Eggs fertilized by sperm having an X-chromosome become females and those fertilized by sperm that do not have an X-chromosome become males. Do you think the number of chromosomes in the male and female are equal? Due to the involvement of the X-chromosome in the determination of sex, it was designated to be the sex chromosome, and the rest of the chromosomes were named as autosomes.Grasshopper is an example of XO type of sex determination in which the males have only one X-chromosome besides the autosomes, whereas females have a pair of X-chromosomes.

132951.subject: Zoology
132951.text: Which of the following groups consists exclusively of placental mammals that exhibit convergent evolution with corresponding Australian marsupials?
132951.sol:
According to the concept of convergent evolution, placental mammals exhibit adaptive radiation in evolving into varieties of such placental mammals each of which appears to be similar to a corresponding Australian marsupial.

Based on the examples provided in NCERT:
- Lemur, Bobcat, and Anteater are all placental mammals.
- Numbat, Spotted cuscus, Flying phalanger, and Tasmanian tiger cat are Australian marsupials.

Option 1 contains only placental mammals (Lemur, Bobcat, Anteater).
Option 2 is incorrect because Numbat is a marsupial.
Option 3 is incorrect because all three (Numbat, Spotted cuscus, Flying phalanger) are marsupials.
Option 4 is incorrect because Tasmanian tiger cat is a marsupial.

Answer: Lemur, Bobcat, Anteater

133400.text:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Proto-oncogenes are normal cellular genes that can become cancerous when mutated.
Reason: Proto-oncogenes are always harmful and lead directly to cancer when expressed.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
133400.sol: After getting into the body of the person, the virus enters into macrophages where RNA genome of the virus replicates to form viral DNA with the help of the enzyme reverse transcriptase. This viral DNA gets incorporated into host cell’s DNA and directs the infected cells to produce virus particles (Figure 7.6). The macrophages continue to produce virus and in this way acts like a HIV factory. Simultaneously, HIV enters into helper T-lymphocytes (TH ), replicates and produce progeny viruses. The progeny viruses released in the blood attack other helper T-lymphocytes. This is repeated leading to a progressive decrease in the number of helper T-lymphocytes in the body of the infected person. During this period, the person suffers from bouts of fever, diarrhoea and weight loss. Due to decrease in the number of helper T lymphocytes, the person starts suffering from infections that could have been otherwise overcome such as those due to bacteria especially Mycobacterium, viruses, fungi and even parasites like Toxoplasma. The patient becomes so immuno-deficient that he/she is unable to protect himself/herself against these infections. A widely used diagnostic test for AIDS is enzyme linked immuno-sorbent assay (ELISA). Treatment of AIDS with anti-retroviral drugs is only partially effective. They can only prolong the life of the patient but cannot prevent death, which is inevitable.

134156.text: What is the purpose of toxicity testing in transgenic animals?
options: To test the safety of vaccines
To study the regulation of genes
To determine the effects of toxic substances
134156.sol: Biological products: Medicines required to treat certain human diseases can contain biological products, but such products are often expensive to make. Transgenic animals that produce useful biological products can be created by the introduction of the portion of DNA (or genes) which codes for a particular product such as human protein (α-1-antitrypsin) used to treat emphysema. Similar attempts are being made for treatment of phenylketonuria (PKU) and cystic fibrosis. In 1997, the first transgenic cow, Rosie, produced human protein-enriched milk (2.4 grams per litre). The milk contained the human alpha-lactalbumin and was nutritionally a more balanced product for human babies than natural cow-milk. (iv) Vaccine safety: Transgenic mice are being developed for use in testing the safety of vaccines before they are used on humans. Transgenic mice are being used to test the safety of the polio vaccine. If successful and found to be reliable, they could replace the use of monkeys to test the safety of batches of the vaccine. (v) Chemical safety testing: This is known as toxicity/safety testing.The procedure is the same as that used for testing toxicity of drugs.Transgenic animals are made that carry genes which make them moresensitive to toxic substances than non-transgenic animals. They are then exposed to the toxic substances and the effects studied. Toxicity testing in such animals will allow us to obtain results in less time

135429.subject: Zoology
135429.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth model is considered a more realistic model than the exponential growth model.
Reason (R): Resources for growth for most animal populations are finite and become limiting sooner or later.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is not correct.
Assertion (A) is not correct but Reason (R) is correct.
135429.sol:
According to the principles of population ecology, no population of any species in nature has at its disposal unlimited resources to permit exponential growth indefinitely. This leads to competition between individuals for limited resources, eventually resulting in a carrying capacity.

Since resources for growth for most animal populations are finite and become limiting sooner or later, the logistic growth model (which incorporates environmental resistance and carrying capacity) is considered a more realistic one compared to the exponential model.

Therefore, both the Assertion and the Reason are correct statements, and the Reason provides the exact biological explanation for why the logistic model is more realistic.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

301811.sol:
Let the observations be ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, {x}_{3}, \ldots , {x}_{50} and the mean be $\overset{¯}{x}$.

From the given data,

Variance~$= 7$, the number of observations \left(n\right) = 50$.

Variance~$= \dfrac{1}{n} ∑ \left({x}_{i} - \overset{¯}{x}\right)2$

$⇒ 7 = \dfrac{1}{50} ∑ \left({x}_{i} - \overset{¯}{x}\right)$2$

$⇒ 350 = ∑ \left({x}_{i} - \overset{¯}{x}\right)2 . . . \left(1\right)$~

Each observation is multiplied by $6$ and then $5$ is~subtracted.

Let the new observations be ${y}_{1}, {y}_{2}, {y}_{3}, \ldots , {y}_{50}$.

${y}_{i} = 6{x}_{i} - 5$

${x}_{i} = $\dfrac{{y}_{i} + 5}{6} . . . \left(2\right)$~

The new variance~$= $\dfrac{1}{n}$∑ \left({y}_{i} - \overset{¯}{y}\right)2$

$\overset{¯}{y} = $\dfrac{1}{n}$∑ {y}_{i} . . . \left(3\right)$~

$⇒ \overset{¯}{y} = \dfrac{1}{50}∑ \left(6{x}_{i} - 5\right)$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{y} = $\dfrac{1}{50}$∑ 6{x}_{i} - \mathop{∑}_{0}^{50}\dfrac{1}{50} $\cdot5$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{y} = $\dfrac{1}{50}$∑ 6{x}_{i} - 5$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{y} = 6\overset{¯}{x} - 5$~ ~[$∴$~From \left(1\right)$]

$⇒ \overset{¯}{x} = $\dfrac{\overset{¯}{y} + 5}{6} . . . \left(4\right)$~

$⇒ ∑ \left({x}_{i} - \overset{¯}{x}\right)2 = 350$

$⇒ ∑ \$left(\dfrac{{y}_{i} + 5}{6} - \dfrac{\overset{¯}{y} + 5}{6}\right)$2 = 350$~ [$∴$ From \left($2\right) \text{ and } \left(4\right)$]

$⇒ ∑ \left(\dfrac{1}{6}\rright)2 \left({y}_{i} - \overset{¯}{y}\right)2 = 350$

$⇒ ∑ \left({y}_{i} - \overset{¯}{y}\right)2 = 36 \times350$

$⇒ ∑ \left({y}_{i} - \overset{¯}{y}\right)2 = 12600$

New variance$= \dfrac{1}{50}∑ \left({y}_{i} - \overset{¯}{y}\right)2 = \dfrac{1}{50} \times12600 = 252

302251.text: An artificial satellite with a metal surface is moving about the earth in a circular orbit. A current will be induced in the satellite, if&

the plane of the orbit is inclined to the plane of the equator.

According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, EMF will be generated across the ends of the conductor when the magnetic flux through a loop of the conductor will change with respect to time.

When the orbit of the satellite is inclined to the equator of the earth, the distance from poles and hence magnitude of the magnetic field due to earth will change at different positions of orbit.

This causes a change in magnetic flux across the metal plate of the satellite and EMF will be generated.

303750.text: In a double slit experiment, a plate having thickness $t$ and refractive index $\mu$ is positioned in front of one of the slits. Determine the change in the optical path resulting from the introduction of the plate.
303750.sol:
When a light ray passes through a medium of thickness $t$ and refractive index $\mu$, the optical path length is $\mu t$.

In the absence of the plate, the optical path length for the same distance in vacuum (or air) is $t$.

The change in the optical path due to the introduction of the plate is the difference between the optical path with the plate and the optical path without the plate.

Change in optical path $= \mu t - t = (\mu - 1)t$.

304045.subject: Physics
304045.text: A steel wire and a copper wire, both possessing equal length and equal cross-sectional area, are joined end to end and the combination is subjected to a tension. Determine the ratio of the strain developed in the copper wire to the strain developed in the steel wire. Let $Y$ of steel $= 2 \times 10^{11} \text{ N/m}^2$ and $Y$ of copper $= 1.3 \times 10^{11} \text{ N/m}^2$.
304045.sol:
Let $F$ be the tension applied to the combination of the wires. Since the wires are joined end to end, the tension $F$ is the same in both wires.

The cross-sectional area $A$ is also the same for both wires. Therefore, the stress $\sigma = \dfrac{F}{A}$ is equal for both the steel and copper wires.

Young's modulus is given by $Y = \dfrac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}}$, which implies $\text{Strain} = \dfrac{\text{Stress}}{Y}$.

Let $\epsilon_c$ and $\epsilon_s$ be the strains developed in the copper and steel wires, respectively.

$\epsilon_c = \dfrac{\sigma}{Y_c}$

$\epsilon_s = \dfrac{\sigma}{Y_s}$

Taking the ratio of the strain in copper to the strain in steel:

$\dfrac{\epsilon_c}{\epsilon_s} = \dfrac{Y_s}{Y_c}$

Substituting the given values, $Y_s = 2 \times 10^{11} \text{ N/m}^2$ and $Y_c = 1.3 \times 10^{11} \text{ N/m}^2$:

$\dfrac{\epsilon_c}{\epsilon_s} = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{11}}{1.3 \times 10^{11}} = \dfrac{20}{13}$

304080.subject: Physics
304080.text: Using the following data, estimate the speed of vertically falling raindrops: radius of the drops $= 0.02 \text{ cm}$, viscosity of air $= 1.8 \times 10^{-4} \text{ poise}$, $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$, and density of water $= 1000 \text{ kg/m}^3$.
304080.sol:
The terminal velocity $v_t$ of a spherical drop falling through a viscous medium is given by Stokes' law:

$v_t = \dfrac{2}{9} \dfrac{r^2 (\rho - \sigma) g}{\eta}$

Given:
Radius of the raindrop, $r = 0.02 \text{ cm} = 2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$
Density of water, $\rho = 1000 \text{ kg/m}^3$
Density of air, $\sigma \approx 0$ (negligible compared to water)
Viscosity of air, $\eta = 1.8 \times 10^{-4} \text{ poise} = 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \text{ Pa}\cdot\text{s}$ (since $1 \text{ poise} = 0.1 \text{ Pa}\cdot\text{s}$)
Acceleration due to gravity, $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$

Substituting the values into the formula:

$v_t = \dfrac{2}{9} \times \dfrac{(2 \times 10^{-4})^2 \times 1000 \times 10}{1.8 \times 10^{-5}}$

$v_t = \dfrac{2}{9} \times \dfrac{4 \times 10^{-8} \times 10^4}{1.8 \times 10^{-5}}$

$v_t = \dfrac{8 \times 10^{-4}}{16.2 \times 10^{-5}}$

$v_t = \dfrac{80}{16.2} \approx 4.94 \text{ m/s}$

Rounding to the nearest integer, the speed of the vertically falling raindrops is approximately $5 \text{ m/s}$.

304658.text: As a wave generated by a boat passes by, a cork floating in a calm pond undergoes simple harmonic motion with frequency $\nu$. The frequency of the wave is
304658.sol:
When a wave propagates through a medium, the particles of the medium execute simple harmonic motion. The frequency of oscillation of the particles is exactly equal to the frequency of the wave.

Since the cork is floating on the water, it acts like a particle of the medium and oscillates up and down with the same frequency as the wave.

Given that the frequency of the simple harmonic motion of the cork is $\nu$, the frequency of the wave must also be $\nu$.

304920.subject: Physics
304920.text: For a body undergoing pure rotation, its axis of rotation
options: can pass through a particle of the body
necessarily passes through the centre of mass
can pass through the centre of mass
necessarily passes through a particle of the body
304920.sol:
For a body undergoing pure rotation, the axis of rotation is the line about which all particles of the body revolve in circular paths.

The axis of rotation can be located anywhere depending on the physical constraints.

It can pass through the centre of mass (for example, a uniform disc rotating about its central axis).

It is not necessary for the axis to pass through the centre of mass (for example, a rod pivoted at one end).

The axis can pass through a particle of the body (for example, a solid sphere rotating about its diameter).

It is not necessary for the axis to pass through a particle of the body (for example, a ring rotating about its central axis, where the axis passes through empty space).

Therefore, the axis of rotation can pass through a particle of the body and can pass through the centre of mass.

305327.text: Two discharge tubes possess identical material structure and are filled with the same gas. The length of one tube is $10 \text{ cm}$ while that of the second tube is $20 \text{ cm}$. Sparking initiates in both tubes when the potential difference between the cathode and the anode reaches $100 \text{ V}$. If the pressure in the shorter tube is $1.0 \text{ mm}$ of mercury, determine the pressure in the longer tube.
305327.sol:
According to Paschen's law, the sparking potential $V$ of a gas between two electrodes depends only on the product of the gas pressure $p$ and the distance $d$ between the electrodes.

$V = f(pd)$

Since the sparking potential is the same for both tubes, the product of pressure and length must be constant.

$p_1 d_1 = p_2 d_2$

Substituting the given values $p_1 = 1.0 \text{ mm}$ of Hg, $d_1 = 10 \text{ cm}$, and $d_2 = 20 \text{ cm}$:

$1.0 \times 10 = p_2 \times 20$

$p_2 = \dfrac{10}{20} = 0.5 \text{ mm}$ of Hg

305488.text: Two rails of a railway track, insulated from both each other and the ground, are connected to a millivoltmeter. Determine the reading of the millivoltmeter when a train travels on the track at a speed of $180 \text{ km h}^{-1}$. The vertical component of the earth's magnetic field is $0.2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ T}$ and the rails are separated by $1 \text{ m}$.
305488.sol:
The speed of the train is $v = 180 \text{ km h}^{-1} = 180 \times \dfrac{5}{18} \text{ m s}^{-1} = 50 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

The axle of the train acts as a conductor of length $l = 1 \text{ m}$ moving with velocity $v$ perpendicular to the vertical component of the earth's magnetic field $B_v$.

The induced motional emf across the axle is given by:

$E = B_v l v$

Substituting the given values:

$E = (0.2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ T}) \times (1 \text{ m}) \times (50 \text{ m s}^{-1})$

$E = 10 \times 10^{-4} \text{ V}$

$E = 10^{-3} \text{ V} = 1 \text{ mV}$

The reading of the millivoltmeter is $1 \text{ mV}$.

305613.text: A nonconducting sheet with a large surface area and a thickness $d$ contains a uniform charge distribution of density $ho$. Determine the electric field at a point $P$ located inside the plate, at a distance $x$ from the central plane, and identify the qualitative shape of the graph of $E$ against $x$ for $0 < x < d$.
options: $\dfrac{\rho x}{2\varepsilon_0}$; linearly increasing for $0 < x < \dfrac{d}{2}$, then constant for $\dfrac{d}{2} \le x < d$
$\dfrac{\rho x}{\varepsilon_0}$; linearly increasing for $0 < x < \dfrac{d}{2}$, then constant for $\dfrac{d}{2} \le x < d$
$\dfrac{\rho x}{2\varepsilon_0}$; linearly increasing for the entire range $0 < x < d$
$\dfrac{\rho x}{\varepsilon_0}$; linearly increasing for the entire range $0 < x < d$
305613.sol:
Consider a Gaussian pillbox symmetric about the central plane of the sheet, with cross-sectional area $A$ and extending to a distance $x$ on both sides.

For a point inside the sheet ($0 < x < \dfrac{d}{2}$):
The charge enclosed by the Gaussian surface is $q_{\text{enclosed}} = \rho (2xA)$.
Using Gauss's law, $\oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{A} = \dfrac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}$
$E(2A) = \dfrac{\rho (2xA)}{\varepsilon_0}$
$E = \dfrac{\rho x}{\varepsilon_0}$
Thus, the electric field increases linearly with $x$ for $0 < x < \dfrac{d}{2}$.

For a point outside the sheet ($x \ge \dfrac{d}{2}$):
The total charge enclosed by the Gaussian surface is $q_{\text{enclosed}} = \rho (dA)$.
Using Gauss's law, $E(2A) = \dfrac{\rho (dA)}{\varepsilon_0}$
$E = \dfrac{\rho d}{2\varepsilon_0}$
Thus, the electric field becomes constant for $x \ge \dfrac{d}{2}$.

Therefore, the graph of $E$ against $x$ is linearly increasing for $0 < x < \dfrac{d}{2}$ and constant for $\dfrac{d}{2} \le x < d$.

306719.subject: Physics
306719.text: A conducting loop is positioned within a uniform magnetic field such that its plane is perpendicular to the field. An emf is induced in the loop if
options: it is rotated about its axis
it is rotated about a diameter
306719.sol:
The magnetic flux linked with the loop is given by $\Phi = \vec{B} \cdot \vec{A} = BA \cos \theta$, where $B$ is the uniform magnetic field, $A$ is the area of the loop, and $\theta$ is the angle between the magnetic field and the area vector.

According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, an emf is induced in the loop if the magnetic flux changes with time.

When the loop is deformed, its area $A$ changes, leading to a change in magnetic flux. Hence, an emf is induced.

When the loop is rotated about its axis, the angle $\theta$ remains constant, and the area $A$ remains constant. The flux does not change, so no emf is induced.

When the loop is rotated about a diameter, the angle $\theta$ changes continuously, leading to a change in magnetic flux. Hence, an emf is induced.

When the loop is translated in a uniform magnetic field, $B$, $A$, and $\theta$ all remain constant. The flux does not change, so no emf is induced.

306810.subject: Physics
306810.text: Suppose $Q$ and $W$ denote the amount of heat supplied to an ideal gas and the work performed by it during an isothermal process. Which of the following relations holds true?
306810.sol:
According to the first law of thermodynamics, $Q = \Delta U + W$.

For an ideal gas, the internal energy depends only on its absolute temperature.

In an isothermal process, the temperature of the gas remains constant, which implies $\Delta T = 0$.

Consequently, the change in internal energy $\Delta U = 0$.

Substituting this into the first law equation yields $Q = W$.

Thus, the heat supplied to the ideal gas is equal to the work performed by it.

307021.text:
Directions: In the given question, a word has been mentioned and there are three ways in which the word has been used in either similar or different ways. You are required to check which of the sentences have correctly used the highlighted word, and mark that as your answer.
Change

I. Social structures will& change soon enough and the purpose of education will finally be to learn to reason and find one's passion.

II. The negotiations would lead to a change of lands between the parties in the presence of the judge to put an end to the dispute.

III. I asked the conductor to keep the change because I despise carrying loose coins in my purse.
307021.sol:
Sentence I.& Social structures will& change soon enough and the purpose of education will finally be to learn to reason and find one's passion.

Here Change means to become different; alter; vary. The usage is correct.

Sentence II. The negotiations would lead to a change of lands between the parties in the presence of the judge to put an end to the dispute.

In this sentence, change has been used which makes no sense. Instead of change, exchange should have been used as it means an act of giving one thing and receiving another (especially of the same kind) in return.

Sentence III.& I asked the conductor to keep the change because I despise carrying loose coins in my purse.

Here the word Change means coins of small denomination which is correctly used in the sentence.
Only I and III are correct.

Option B is hence the correct answer.

309002.subject: Chemistry
309002.text: Identify the appropriate reaction conditions for the transformations A, B, and C shown in the following scheme:
options: A: Oxymercuration-demercuration; B: Acid-catalysed hydration; C: Hydroboration-oxidation
A: Acid-catalysed hydration; B: Hydroboration-oxidation; C: Oxymercuration-demercuration
A: Hydroboration-oxidation; B: Oxymercuration-demercuration; C: Acid-catalysed hydration
A: Oxymercuration-demercuration; B: Hydroboration-oxidation; C: Acid-catalysed hydration
309002.sol:
The starting material is vinylcyclohexane.

Transformation A yields 2-cyclohexylethanol. This is an anti-Markovnikov addition of water across the double bond, which is achieved by hydroboration-oxidation.

Transformation B yields 1-cyclohexylethanol. This is a Markovnikov addition of water without any skeletal rearrangement, which is achieved by oxymercuration-demercuration.

Transformation C yields 1-ethylcyclohexanol. This product is formed via a carbocation rearrangement, characteristic of acid-catalysed hydration. Protonation of the alkene forms a secondary carbocation at the carbon adjacent to the ring. A $1,2$-hydride shift from the tertiary ring carbon generates a more stable tertiary carbocation, which is then attacked by water to form the tertiary alcohol.

Thus, A is Hydroboration-oxidation, B is Oxymercuration-demercuration, and C is Acid-catalysed hydration.

Answer: A: Hydroboration-oxidation; B: Oxymercuration-demercuration; C: Acid-catalysed hydration

309152.subject: Chemistry
309152.text: Aldehydes and ketones react with $\alpha$-bromo esters and zinc metal in an ether or benzene medium to yield:
309152.sol:
The reaction of aldehydes or ketones with $\alpha$-bromo esters and zinc metal in an ether or benzene medium is known as the Reformatsky reaction.

Zinc reacts with the $\alpha$-bromo ester to form an organozinc intermediate, which is a zinc enolate.

This intermediate acts as a nucleophile and attacks the carbonyl carbon of the aldehyde or ketone to form a zinc alkoxide.

Upon acidic hydrolysis, the zinc alkoxide yields a $\beta$-hydroxy ester.

The general reaction is:

$R_2C=O + Br-CH_2-COOR' + Zn \xrightarrow{\text{ether}} R_2C(OZnBr)-CH_2-COOR'$

$R_2C(OZnBr)-CH_2-COOR' \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} R_2C(OH)-CH_2-COOR'$

The final product is a $\beta$-hydroxy ester.

Answer: $\beta$-hydroxy esters

309473.subject: Chemistry
309473.text:
Arrange the following compounds in decreasing order of their reactivity towards electrophilic addition of $\mathrm{Br}_{2}$ in $\mathrm{CHCl}_{3}$:
(I) $\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CO}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{3}$
(II) $\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$
(III) $\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$
309473.sol:
The reactivity of an alkene towards electrophilic addition of $\mathrm{Br}_{2}$ depends on the electron density of the carbon-carbon double bond. Higher electron density makes the alkene more nucleophilic, thereby increasing its reactivity towards electrophiles.

Electron-donating groups (EDG) increase the electron density of the double bond, while electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) decrease it.

Analyzing the given compounds:
(III) $\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$: The $-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$ group is a strong electron-donating group due to its $+M$ (resonance) effect, which significantly increases the electron density on the double bond.
(II) $\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$: The $-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$ group is an electron-donating group due to hyperconjugation and $+I$ (inductive) effect, which moderately increases the electron density.
(I) $\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CO}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{3}$: The $-\mathrm{CO}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{3}$ group is a strong electron-withdrawing group due to its $-M$ and $-I$ effects, which decreases the electron density on the double bond.

Since the $+M$ effect of $-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$ is stronger than the hyperconjugation of $-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$, the electron density of the double bond follows the order: (III) > (II) > (I).

Therefore, the decreasing order of reactivity towards electrophilic addition of $\mathrm{Br}_{2}$ is (III) > (II) > (I).

Answer: (III) > (II) > (I)

309492.subject: Chemistry
309492.text:
The relative yield of the following alkenes produced by the reaction of trans-1-chloro-2-methylcyclohexane with KOH and heat is:

(i) 1-Methylcyclohexene
(ii) Methylenecyclohexane
(iii) 3-Methylcyclohexene
309492.sol:
The reaction of an alkyl halide with KOH and heat proceeds via the E2 elimination mechanism.

E2 elimination in cyclohexanes requires an anti-periplanar geometry between the leaving group (Cl) and the $\beta$-hydrogen. This means both must occupy axial positions in the chair conformation.

In trans-1-chloro-2-methylcyclohexane, the molecule exists in an equilibrium between the diequatorial (e,e) and diaxial (a,a) conformations. For E2 elimination to occur, the ring must adopt the conformation where the Cl atom is axial. In this conformation, the methyl group at C2 is also axial.

Looking at the $\beta$-carbons (C2 and C6):
At C2, the methyl group is axial, which means the $\beta$-hydrogen is equatorial. Since it is not axial, it cannot undergo anti-periplanar elimination with the axial Cl. Thus, the formation of 1-methylcyclohexene (i) is highly restricted.

At C6, there are two hydrogens (one axial and one equatorial). The axial hydrogen at C6 is anti-periplanar to the axial Cl at C1. Elimination readily occurs between C1 and C6, yielding 3-methylcyclohexene (iii) as the major product.

Methylenecyclohexane (ii) has an exocyclic double bond, which would require the loss of a hydrogen from a methyl group attached to C1. Since the methyl group is at C2, this product cannot be formed under E2 conditions without rearrangement, making its yield zero.

Therefore, the relative yield of the alkenes is 3-Methylcyclohexene > 1-Methylcyclohexene > Methylenecyclohexane, which corresponds to (iii) > (i) > (ii).

Answer: (iii) > (i) > (ii)

309534.subject: Chemistry
309534.text:
Arrange the following compounds in decreasing order of their acidic strength (increasing $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ values):

(I)
(II)
(III)
(IV)
309534.sol:
The given compounds are:
(I) Formic acid ($\text{HCOOH}$)
(II) Oxalic acid ($\text{HOOC}-\text{COOH}$)
(III) Malonic acid ($\text{HOOC}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}$)
(IV) Acetic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$)

Acidic strength depends on the stability of the conjugate base formed after the removal of an $\text{H}^+$ ion. Electron-withdrawing groups ($-I$ effect) stabilize the carboxylate anion by dispersing the negative charge, thereby increasing acidity. Conversely, electron-donating groups ($+I$ effect) destabilize the anion, decreasing acidity.

In oxalic acid (II), the strongly electron-withdrawing $-\text{COOH}$ group is directly attached to the ionizing carboxyl group, exerting a very strong $-I$ effect. Thus, it is the strongest acid.

In malonic acid (III), the $-\text{COOH}$ group is separated by a $-\text{CH}_2-$ group. The $-I$ effect decreases with distance, making it a weaker acid than oxalic acid but stronger than formic acid.

Formic acid (I) has a hydrogen atom attached to the carboxyl group, which serves as the reference (no $+I$ or $-I$ effect).

Acetic acid (IV) has a methyl group ($-\text{CH}_3$) which exerts a $+I$ effect, destabilizing the conjugate base and making it the weakest acid among the four.

Therefore, the decreasing order of acidic strength is (II) > (III) > (I) > (IV).

Answer: (II) > (III) > (I) > (IV)

309659.subject: Chemistry
309659.text: An aromatic compound (A) with the molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_{7}\mathrm{H}_{6}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ gives a precipitate of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ on boiling with an alcoholic $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$ solution, and yields a compound of formula $\mathrm{C}_{7}\mathrm{H}_{7}\mathrm{OCl}$ on treatment with aqueous sodium hydroxide. Oxidation of (A) gives a monochlorobenzoic acid which affords only one mononitro derivative upon nitration. Compound (A) is:
309659.sol:
Compound (A) has the molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_{7}\mathrm{H}_{6}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$.

It gives a precipitate of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ on boiling with alcoholic $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$ solution, which indicates the presence of a benzylic chlorine atom (reactive towards nucleophilic substitution).

Treatment with aqueous $\mathrm{NaOH}$ yields a compound with the formula $\mathrm{C}_{7}\mathrm{H}_{7}\mathrm{OCl}$. This means only one chlorine atom is replaced by an $-\mathrm{OH}$ group, confirming that one chlorine is benzylic and the other is attached directly to the benzene ring (aryl chlorine, which is unreactive under these conditions). Thus, (A) is a chlorobenzyl chloride.

Oxidation of (A) gives a monochlorobenzoic acid. The position of the chlorine atom on the ring remains unchanged.

Nitration of this monochlorobenzoic acid yields only one mononitro derivative. Let us analyze the possible isomers:
1. $o$-chlorobenzoic acid: The $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group directs to the meta positions (3 and 5), and the $-\mathrm{Cl}$ group directs to the ortho/para positions (3 and 5). Since positions 3 and 5 are not equivalent, nitration gives a mixture of two products.
2. $m$-chlorobenzoic acid: The directing effects of $-\mathrm{COOH}$ and $-\mathrm{Cl}$ lead to multiple non-equivalent positions, resulting in a mixture of products.
3. $p$-chlorobenzoic acid: The $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group directs to positions 3 and 5. The $-\mathrm{Cl}$ group also directs to positions 3 and 5 (ortho to $-\mathrm{Cl}$). Because the molecule has a plane of symmetry passing through C1 and C4, positions 3 and 5 are identical. Therefore, nitration yields only one product (4-chloro-3-nitrobenzoic acid).

Since only $p$-chlorobenzoic acid gives a single mononitro derivative, the original compound (A) must be $p$-chlorobenzyl chloride.

Answer:

So number of triplets $=\frac{3!}{2!}=3$

6a0e277a165ae1327797b3f3.subject: Biology
6a0e277a165ae1327797b3f3.text: In Rana tigrina, which of the following external morphological features is exclusively present in males and helps in distinguishing them from females?
options: Membranous tympanum on either side of the eyes
Webbed digits in the hind limbs
6a0e277a165ae1327797b3f3.sol:
In Rana tigrina (Indian bullfrog), male frogs can be distinguished from female frogs by the presence of sound producing vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimbs.

Membranous tympanum, webbed digits in the hind limbs, and nictitating membrane are present in both male and female frogs.

Answer: Sound producing vocal sacs

6a104ffc8b46719ce7976d47.subject: Biology
6a104ffc8b46719ce7976d47.text: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids of varied shapes and sizes that store different types of nutrients. Which of the following types of leucoplasts is specifically responsible for storing oils and fats?
6a104ffc8b46719ce7976d47.sol:
Plastids are classified based on the type of pigments or food they store.

Leucoplasts are colourless plastids which store nutrients. They are of three main types:

Amyloplasts store carbohydrates (starch), for example, in potato.

Elaioplasts store oils and fats.

Aleuroplasts store proteins.

Chromoplasts are coloured plastids containing fat-soluble carotenoid pigments like carotene and xanthophylls, which give colour to plant parts.

Therefore, elaioplasts are the specific leucoplasts responsible for storing oils and fats.

Answer: Elaioplasts

6a104ffe8b46719ce7976d72.subject: Biology
6a104ffe8b46719ce7976d72.text:
Regarding the mechanism of competitive inhibition of an enzyme, arrange the following events in the correct logical sequence of cause and effect :
A. The inhibitor competes with the substrate for the substrate-binding site.
B. Decline in the overall enzyme action.
C. Introduction of an inhibitor that closely resembles the substrate in molecular structure.
D. The normal substrate is prevented from binding to the enzyme.
E. The inhibitor binds to the active site of the enzyme.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
6a104ffe8b46719ce7976d72.sol:
In competitive inhibition, the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure.

First, the inhibitor is introduced into the system (C).

Due to its structural similarity, the inhibitor competes with the normal substrate for the substrate-binding site (A).

As a result of this competition, the inhibitor binds to the active site of the enzyme (E).

This binding physically blocks the active site, preventing the normal substrate from binding to the enzyme (D).

Consequently, the rate of the enzyme-catalyzed reaction decreases, leading to a decline in overall enzyme action (B).

The correct logical sequence is C, A, E, D, B.

Answer: $C, A, E, D, B$

6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fba.subject: Biology
6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fba.text: If in a pond there were $50$ water lily plants last year and through reproduction $15$ new plants are added this year, the birth rate in the population is ____ offspring per water lily per year.
6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fba.sol:
Initial population of water lily plants, $N = 50$

Number of new plants added through reproduction, $\Delta N = 15$

Time period, $\Delta t = 1$ year

Birth rate is calculated as the number of new individuals produced per unit of the initial population per unit time.

Birth rate $= \dfrac{\Delta N}{N \times \Delta t}$

Birth rate $= \dfrac{15}{50 \times 1} = 0.3$ offspring per water lily per year.

Answer: $0.3$

6a7a1ff8df60aec2b5fce6d6.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff8df60aec2b5fce6d6.text: A physical quantity is defined as $X = L^x C^y R^z$, where $L$, $C$, and $R$ are self-inductance, capacitance, and resistance respectively, and $x, y, z$ are non-zero real numbers. If $X$ is found to be entirely independent of the fundamental dimension of electric current $[A]$, what must be true about its dependence on the dimensions of mass $[M]$ and length $[L]$?
options: $X$ depends on both mass and length.
$X$ is independent of both mass and length.
$X$ depends on mass but is independent of length.
$X$ depends on length but is independent of mass.
6a7a1ff8df60aec2b5fce6d6.sol:
The dimensional formulas for the given quantities are:
$[L] = [M L^2 T^{-2} A^{-2}]$
$[C] = [M^{-1} L^{-2} T^4 A^2]$
$[R] = [M L^2 T^{-3} A^{-2}]$

For the quantity $X = L^x C^y R^z$, the combined dimensional formula is:
$[X] = [M L^2 T^{-2} A^{-2}]^x [M^{-1} L^{-2} T^4 A^2]^y [M L^2 T^{-3} A^{-2}]^z$

Grouping the fundamental dimensions:
$[X] = [M^{x - y + z} L^{2x - 2y + 2z} T^{-2x + 4y - 3z} A^{-2x + 2y - 2z}]$

It is given that $X$ is independent of the dimension of electric current $[A]$. Therefore, the exponent of $A$ must be zero:
$-2x + 2y - 2z = 0 \Rightarrow y = x + z$

Now, substitute $y = x + z$ into the exponents of mass $[M]$ and length $[L]$:
Exponent of $M = x - y + z = x - (x + z) + z = 0$
Exponent of $L = 2x - 2y + 2z = 2(x - y + z) = 2(0) = 0$

Since the exponents of both $[M]$ and $[L]$ evaluate to zero, the quantity $X$ must be independent of both mass and length.

Answer: $X$ is independent of both mass and length.

6a7a1ff865a6c69b0a1c6712.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff865a6c69b0a1c6712.text:
A block is projected upwards along a rough inclined plane with an initial speed of $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The angle of inclination of the plane is $37^{\circ}$. If the block travels a distance of $5\text{ m}$ up the incline before momentarily coming to rest, the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline is:
(Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, $\sin 37^{\circ} = \dfrac{3}{5}$, $\cos 37^{\circ} = \dfrac{4}{5}$)
6a7a1ff865a6c69b0a1c6712.sol:
Using the kinematic equation for uniform acceleration:
$v^2 = u^2 - 2as$

Given $u = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $v = 0$, and $s = 5\text{ m}$:
$0 = (10)^2 - 2 \times a \times 5$
$10a = 100 \Rightarrow a = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$

For a block sliding up a rough inclined plane, the net deceleration is provided by the component of gravity and the kinetic friction acting downwards along the incline:
$m a = m g \sin \theta + \mu_k m g \cos \theta$
$a = g (\sin \theta + \mu_k \cos \theta)$

Substituting the given values:
$10 = 10 \left(\dfrac{3}{5} + \mu_k \times \dfrac{4}{5}\right)$
$1 = 0.6 + 0.8 \mu_k$
$0.8 \mu_k = 0.4$
$\mu_k = \dfrac{0.4}{0.8} = 0.5$

Answer: $0.5$

6a7a1ff8dfd1d1515ab27c2c.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff8dfd1d1515ab27c2c.text: A large liquid drop is broken into $N$ identical smaller droplets. If the total surface energy of the system increases by $300\%$ during this process, the value of $N$ is:
6a7a1ff8dfd1d1515ab27c2c.sol:
Let the radius of the large drop be $R$ and the radius of each small droplet be $r$.

By conservation of volume:
$\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = N \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\right) \Rightarrow R = N^{1/3} r$

The initial surface energy is $U_i = 4\pi R^2 T$.

The final total surface energy is:
$U_f = N(4\pi r^2 T) = N \left(4\pi \left(\dfrac{R}{N^{1/3}}\right)^2 T\right) = N^{1/3} (4\pi R^2 T) = N^{1/3} U_i$

Given that the surface energy increases by $300\%$, the final surface energy is:
$U_f = U_i + \dfrac{300}{100} U_i = 4 U_i$

Equating the two expressions for $U_f$:
$N^{1/3} U_i = 4 U_i \Rightarrow N^{1/3} = 4$

Cubing both sides, we obtain:
$N = 64$

Answer: $64$

6a7a1ff88415536411bac08a.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff88415536411bac08a.text: An open organ pipe and a closed organ pipe have the same inner radius of $5\text{ cm}$. The fundamental frequency of the open pipe is found to be equal to the first overtone frequency of the closed pipe. If the physical length of the open pipe is $24\text{ cm}$, what is the physical length of the closed pipe? (Consider the end correction for the pipes)
6a7a1ff88415536411bac08a.sol:
The end correction $e$ for a pipe of radius $r$ is given by $e = 0.6r$.
Given $r = 5\text{ cm}$, the end correction is $e = 0.6 \times 5 = 3\text{ cm}$.

For the open organ pipe, end correction is applied at both ends. Its effective length is:
$L_{o,\text{eff}} = L_o + 2e = 24 + 2(3) = 30\text{ cm}$.

The fundamental frequency of the open pipe is:
$f_{o,1} = \dfrac{v}{2L_{o,\text{eff}}} = \dfrac{v}{2 \times 30} = \dfrac{v}{60}$

For the closed organ pipe, end correction is applied at one end only. Its effective length is:
$L_{c,\text{eff}} = L_c + e = L_c + 3$

The first overtone of a closed pipe corresponds to the $3^{\text{rd}}$ harmonic. Its frequency is:
$f_{c,3} = \dfrac{3v}{4L_{c,\text{eff}}}$

According to the question, $f_{o,1} = f_{c,3}$:
$\dfrac{v}{60} = \dfrac{3v}{4L_{c,\text{eff}}}$
$\Rightarrow 4L_{c,\text{eff}} = 180$
$\Rightarrow L_{c,\text{eff}} = 45\text{ cm}$

Now, substituting the effective length back to find the physical length:
$L_c + 3 = 45$
$\Rightarrow L_c = 42\text{ cm}$

Answer: $42\text{ cm}$

6a7a1ff8e96b8e77ba2e0cd5.text:
The proton separation energy is the minimum energy required to remove a single proton from a nucleus. For the nucleus $N 14 7$, this separation energy is given as $7 . 452MeV$. If the atomic mass of $C 13 6$ is $13 . 00335u$ and the mass of a hydrogen atom $H 1 1$ is $1 . 00783u$, what is the atomic mass of $N 14 7$?

(Take $1u = 931 . 5MeV / {c}^{2}$)
6a7a1ff8e96b8e77ba2e0cd5.sol:
The nuclear reaction for the removal of a proton is:
$N 14 7 + {E}_{p} \to C 13 6 + H 1 1$

The proton separation energy ${E}_{p}$ is the energy equivalent of the mass defect $\Deltam$:
$\Deltam = \dfrac{{E}_{p}}{931 . 5} = \dfrac{7 . 452}{931 . 5} = 0 . 00800u$

The mass defect is also given by the difference between the sum of the product masses and the mass of the parent nucleus:
$\Deltam = \left[M ( C 13 6 ) + M ( H 1 1 )\right] - M ( N 14 7 )$

Rearranging to solve for the mass of $N 14 7$:
$M ( N 14 7 ) = M ( C 13 6 ) + M ( H 1 1 ) - \Deltam$
$M ( N 14 7 ) = 13 . 00335 + 1 . 00783 - 0 . 00800$
$M ( N 14 7 ) = 14 . 01118 - 0 . 00800 = 14 . 00318u$

Answer: $14 . 00318u$

6a7a1ff885fb14dac87698e1.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff885fb14dac87698e1.text:
A logic circuit has two inputs $A$ and $B$. These inputs are fed simultaneously into an OR gate and a NAND gate. The outputs of these two gates are then connected to the inputs of an unknown logic gate $G$. The final output of the circuit is $X$. The truth table for the circuit is given below:

$A$$B$$X$
000
011
101
110


Identify the logic gate $G$.
6a7a1ff885fb14dac87698e1.sol:
Let the output of the OR gate be $Y_1$ and the output of the NAND gate be $Y_2$.
$Y_1 = A + B$
$Y_2 = \overline{A \cdot B}$

The given truth table corresponds to the XOR operation, where the output $X$ is $1$ only when the inputs $A$ and $B$ are different.
Let us check the outputs $Y_1$ and $Y_2$ for all combinations of $A$ and $B$:
If $A=0, B=0 \Rightarrow Y_1=0, Y_2=1$. We need $X=0$.
If $A=0, B=1 \Rightarrow Y_1=1, Y_2=1$. We need $X=1$.
If $A=1, B=0 \Rightarrow Y_1=1, Y_2=1$. We need $X=1$.
If $A=1, B=1 \Rightarrow Y_1=1, Y_2=0$. We need $X=0$.

Notice that $X$ is exactly the logical AND of $Y_1$ and $Y_2$.
$X = Y_1 \cdot Y_2 = (A + B) \cdot \overline{A \cdot B}$
$X = (A + B) \cdot (\overline{A} + \overline{B}) = A\overline{A} + A\overline{B} + B\overline{A} + B\overline{B} = A\overline{B} + \overline{A}B$
This matches the XOR operation. Therefore, the unknown gate $G$ must be an AND gate.

Answer: AND gate

6a7a1ff84de447105874336e.subject: Chemistry
6a7a1ff84de447105874336e.text:
Consider the following cross-conjugated and related molecules:
(I) Fulvalene (a system of two cross-conjugated five-membered rings)
(II) Sesquifulvalene (a system of a five-membered and a seven-membered cross-conjugated ring)
(III) Heptafulvalene (a system of two cross-conjugated seven-membered rings)
(IV) Bicyclohexylidene (two six-membered saturated rings connected by a double bond)

Which of these molecules is expected to possess the highest permanent dipole moment?
6a7a1ff84de447105874336e.sol:
A high permanent dipole moment in a hydrocarbon arises when a dipolar resonance contributor is exceptionally stable.

For sesquifulvalene (II), heterolytic polarization of the central exocyclic double bond can place a negative charge on the five-membered ring and a positive charge on the seven-membered ring. This results in a cyclopentadienyl anion (6 $\pi$ electrons, aromatic) and a cycloheptatrienyl (tropylium) cation (6 $\pi$ electrons, aromatic). Since both rings become aromatic, this dipolar structure is highly stable and contributes significantly to the resonance hybrid, giving the molecule a large dipole moment.

For fulvalene (I) and heptafulvalene (III), polarization would result in one aromatic ring and one antiaromatic ring, making the dipolar contributor highly unstable and energetically unfavorable.

Bicyclohexylidene (IV) is non-polar as it lacks conjugation and any driving force for charge separation.

Thus, sesquifulvalene (II) has the highest permanent dipole moment.

Answer: (II)

6a7a1ff81104d514316f7b17.subject: Chemistry
6a7a1ff81104d514316f7b17.text: Consider the following oxides formed by elements from the s and p blocks: $\text{SO}_3$, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{CaO}$, and $\text{K}_2\text{O}$. Which of the following represents the correct increasing order of their basic character?
6a7a1ff81104d514316f7b17.sol:
The basic character of an oxide is directly related to the metallic character of its central element. Metallic character increases down a group and decreases across a period from left to right.

The central elements are Sulphur (S), Aluminium (Al), Calcium (Ca), and Potassium (K).
Sulphur is a non-metal, so $\text{SO}_3$ is an acidic oxide.
Aluminium is a metal/metalloid, and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is an amphoteric oxide.
Calcium is a Group 2 metal, so $\text{CaO}$ is a basic oxide.
Potassium is a Group 1 metal, so $\text{K}_2\text{O}$ is a strongly basic oxide.

The increasing order of metallic character is $\text{S} < \text{Al} < \text{Ca} < \text{K}$.
Therefore, the increasing order of basic character of their oxides follows the same trend: $\text{SO}_3 < \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 < \text{CaO} < \text{K}_2\text{O}$.

Answer: $\text{SO}_3 < \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 < \text{CaO} < \text{K}_2\text{O}$

6a7a1ff87254ac4f50ef4ab5.text: Anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ is treated with two different aqueous reagents. In the first reaction, it is dissolved in an acidified aqueous solution to form a complex cation $P$. In the second reaction, it is treated with an excess of aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ to form a soluble complex anion $Q$. The coordination number of aluminium in complexes $P$ and $Q$, respectively, are:
6a7a1ff87254ac4f50ef4ab5.sol:
When $\text{AlCl}_3$ is dissolved in an acidified aqueous solution, it forms the octahedral hexaaquaaluminium(III) ion, $[\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$. Thus, the coordination number of aluminium in complex $P$ is $6$.

When $\text{AlCl}_3$ is treated with an excess of aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, aluminium exhibits amphoteric behaviour and forms a soluble tetrahydroxoaluminate(III) complex, $[\text{Al}(\text{OH})_4]^-$. In this complex $Q$, the coordination number of aluminium is $4$.

Answer: $6$ and $4$

6a7a1ff897438c3e5e8a1974.subject: Mathematics
6a7a1ff897438c3e5e8a1974.text:
Let $f: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function satisfying the relation

$\sum_{k=1}^x f(k) = x^2 f(x) - 2$

for all integers $x \ge 2$. If $\sum_{x=1}^\infty f(x) = 10$, then the value of $f(1)$ is equal to
6a7a1ff897438c3e5e8a1974.sol:
Let $f(1) = \alpha$.

Substitute $x=2$ into the given equation:
$f(1) + f(2) = 4f(2) - 2$
$\alpha + 2 = 3f(2) \Rightarrow f(2) = \dfrac{\alpha + 2}{3}$

For $x \ge 3$, let $S_x = \sum_{k=1}^x f(k)$. We have:
$S_x = x^2 f(x) - 2$
$S_{x-1} = (x-1)^2 f(x-1) - 2$

Subtracting the second equation from the first:
$f(x) = x^2 f(x) - (x-1)^2 f(x-1)$
$(x^2 - 1) f(x) = (x-1)^2 f(x-1)$
$(x+1)f(x) = (x-1)f(x-1)$

Thus, $f(x) = \dfrac{x-1}{x+1} f(x-1)$ for $x \ge 3$.

By telescoping products:
$f(x) = \left( \dfrac{x-1}{x+1} \right) \left( \dfrac{x-2}{x} \right) \dots \left( \dfrac{2}{4} \right) f(2)$

$f(x) = \dfrac{2 \cdot 3}{x(x+1)} f(2) = \dfrac{6}{x(x+1)} \cdot \dfrac{\alpha + 2}{3} = \dfrac{2(\alpha + 2)}{x(x+1)}$

This formula is valid for $x \ge 2$.

The infinite sum is given as $10$:
$\sum_{x=1}^\infty f(x) = f(1) + \sum_{x=2}^\infty f(x) = 10$

Substitute the expressions:
$\alpha + \sum_{x=2}^\infty \dfrac{2(\alpha + 2)}{x(x+1)} = 10$

$\alpha + 2(\alpha + 2) \sum_{x=2}^\infty \left( \dfrac{1}{x} - \dfrac{1}{x+1} \right) = 10$

The series is telescoping:

6a7a1ff8f3ccce0632450be4.text: Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be two complex numbers such that $|z_1| = 2$ and $|z_2| = 3$. If $\arg\left(\dfrac{z_1}{\overline{z}_2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $\arg(z_1 \overline{z}_2) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$, then the exact value of $|z_1 + \overline{z}_2|^2 + |z_1 - z_2|^2$ is
6a7a1ff8f3ccce0632450be4.sol:
Given $\arg\left(\dfrac{z_1}{\overline{z}_2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$\Rightarrow \arg(z_1) - \arg(\overline{z}_2) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$\Rightarrow \arg(z_1) + \arg(z_2) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

Also given $\arg(z_1 \overline{z}_2) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$\Rightarrow \arg(z_1) + \arg(\overline{z}_2) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$\Rightarrow \arg(z_1) - \arg(z_2) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

Now, $|z_1 + \overline{z}_2|^2 = |z_1|^2 + |\overline{z}_2|^2 + 2|z_1||\overline{z}_2|\cos(\arg(z_1) - \arg(\overline{z}_2))$

Since $|\overline{z}_2| = |z_2| = 3$ and $\arg(z_1) - \arg(\overline{z}_2) = \arg(z_1) + \arg(z_2) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$|z_1 + \overline{z}_2|^2 = 2^2 + 3^2 + 2(2)(3)\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 13 + 12\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 19$

Similarly, $|z_1 - z_2|^2 = |z_1|^2 + |z_2|^2 - 2|z_1||z_2|\cos(\arg(z_1) - \arg(z_2))$

$|z_1 - z_2|^2 = 2^2 + 3^2 - 2(2)(3)\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = 13 - 12\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 13 - 6\sqrt{3}$

Therefore, $|z_1 + \overline{z}_2|^2 + |z_1 - z_2|^2 = 19 + 13 - 6\sqrt{3} = 32 - 6\sqrt{3}$

Answer: $32 - 6\sqrt{3}$

6a7a1ff8ba21e14081f69294.text: Let a sequence be defined by $a_1 = 4$ and $a_{k+1} - a_k = 6k + 2$ for all $k \ge 1$. If $S_n = \sum_{k=1}^n a_k$ and $n$ is a positive integer such that $2900 < S_n < 3000$, then the value of $n$ is ____________.
6a7a1ff8ba21e14081f69294.sol:
Given $a_1 = 4$ and $a_{k+1} - a_k = 6k + 2$.

We can find the $k$-th term $a_k$ using the method of differences:
$a_k = a_1 + \sum_{j=1}^{k-1} (a_{j+1} - a_j)$
$a_k = 4 + \sum_{j=1}^{k-1} (6j + 2)$
$a_k = 4 + 6\dfrac{(k-1)k}{2} + 2(k-1)$
$a_k = 4 + 3k^2 - 3k + 2k - 2$
$a_k = 3k^2 - k + 2$

Now, we compute the sum $S_n = \sum_{k=1}^n a_k$ :
$S_n = \sum_{k=1}^n (3k^2 - k + 2)$
$S_n = 3\dfrac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6} - \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2} + 2n$
$S_n = \dfrac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{2} - \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2} + 2n$
$S_n = \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}[2n+1 - 1] + 2n$
$S_n = n^2(n+1) + 2n = n^3 + n^2 + 2n$

We are given that $2900 < S_n < 3000$.
So, $2900 < n^3 + n^2 + 2n < 3000$.

Let us test integer values for $n$.
For $n = 13$: $S_{13} = 13^3 + 13^2 + 2(13) = 2197 + 169 + 26 = 2392$
For $n = 14$: $S_{14} = 14^3 + 14^2 + 2(14) = 2744 + 196 + 28 = 2968$
For $n = 15$: $S_{15} = 15^3 + 15^2 + 2(15) = 3375 + 225 + 30 = 3630$

The only integer satisfying the inequality is $n = 14$.

Answer: $14$

6a7a1ff8a68eacdcf334ea1f.text: If the sum of all solutions of the equation $\log_{2}(\sin x) + \log_{2}(\cos x) = -1$ in the interval $[0, 8\pi]$ is $k\pi$, then the value of $k$ is _______.
6a7a1ff8a68eacdcf334ea1f.sol:
For the given logarithmic equation to be defined, the arguments must be strictly positive:
$\sin x > 0$ and $\cos x > 0$
This restricts the valid solutions to the first quadrant.

Using the properties of logarithms, we can combine the terms:
$\log_{2}(\sin x \cos x) = -1$
$\Rightarrow \sin x \cos x = 2^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Multiplying both sides by 2:
$2\sin x \cos x = 1$
$\Rightarrow \sin(2x) = 1$

The general solution for this is:
$2x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + 2n\pi$
$\Rightarrow x = \dfrac{\pi}{4} + n\pi$, where $n \in \mathbb{Z}$

Since $x$ must lie in the first quadrant, $n$ must be an even integer. Let $n = 2m$, so $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4} + 2m\pi$.

We need to find solutions in the interval $[0, 8\pi]$:
$0 \le \dfrac{\pi}{4} + 2m\pi \le 8\pi$
$0 \le \dfrac{1}{4} + 2m \le 8$
$-0.25 \le 2m \le 7.75$
$-0.125 \le m \le 3.875$

The possible integer values for $m$ are $0, 1, 2,$ and $3$.
The corresponding solutions for $x$ are:
For $m=0, x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$
For $m=1, x = \dfrac{9\pi}{4}$
For $m=2, x = \dfrac{17\pi}{4}$
For $m=3, x = \dfrac{25\pi}{4}$

Sum of these solutions $= \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{9\pi}{4} + \dfrac{17\pi}{4} + \dfrac{25\pi}{4} = \dfrac{52\pi}{4} = 13\pi$.

Comparing this with $k\pi$, we get $k = 13$.

Answer: $13$

6a7a1ff8202f65fd33798b00.text: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} \alpha & \beta \\ \gamma & \delta \end{bmatrix}$ be a $2 \times 2$ real matrix such that $\alpha+\delta=1$ and $\alpha\delta-\beta\gamma=0$. If $(I+A)^5 + (I-A)^5 = \begin{bmatrix} 92 & 60 \\ -90 & -58 \end{bmatrix}$, where $I$ is the $2 \times 2$ identity matrix, then the value of $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 + \gamma^2 + \delta^2$ is:
6a7a1ff8202f65fd33798b00.sol:
We are given that $\text{tr}(A) = \alpha+\delta = 1$ and $\det(A) = \alpha\delta-\beta\gamma = 0$.

By the Cayley-Hamilton theorem, every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation:
$A^2 - \text{tr}(A)A + \det(A)I = 0$
$A^2 - A = 0 \implies A^2 = A$.

Since $A^2 = A$, it follows that $A^k = A$ for all integers $k \ge 1$.

Now, expand $(I+A)^5$ using the binomial theorem:
$(I+A)^5 = I + ^{5}C_{1}A + ^{5}C_{2}A^2 + ^{5}C_{3}A^3 + ^{5}C_{4}A^4 + ^{5}C_{5}A^5$
Since $A^k = A$, this simplifies to:
$(I+A)^5 = I + (5 + 10 + 10 + 5 + 1)A = I + 31A$.

Similarly, expand $(I-A)^5$:
$(I-A)^5 = I - ^{5}C_{1}A + ^{5}C_{2}A^2 - ^{5}C_{3}A^3 + ^{5}C_{4}A^4 - ^{5}C_{5}A^5$
$(I-A)^5 = I + (-5 + 10 - 10 + 5 - 1)A = I - A$.

Adding the two expressions:
$(I+A)^5 + (I-A)^5 = (I + 31A) + (I - A) = 2I + 30A$.

We are given that this sum equals $\begin{bmatrix} 92 & 60 \\ -90 & -58 \end{bmatrix}$.
So, $2I + 30A = \begin{bmatrix} 92 & 60 \\ -90 & -58 \end{bmatrix}$
$30A = \begin{bmatrix} 92 & 60 \\ -90 & -58 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 90 & 60 \\ -90 & -60 \end{bmatrix}$

Dividing by $30$, we get:
$A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ -3 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$.

Thus, $\alpha = 3$, $\beta = 2$, $\gamma = -3$, and $\delta = -2$.

The value of $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 + \gamma^2 + \delta^2$ is:
$3^2 + 2^2 + (-3)^2 + (-2)^2 = 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26$.

Answer: $26$

6a7a1ff88d64bc5514693b17.text: If for some $\alpha \in [0, \pi]$, the relation $x^2 + y^2 - \sqrt{3}xy = \dfrac{1}{4}$ holds for all real numbers $x, y \in (0,1)$ that satisfy $\sin^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}y = \alpha$, then the value of $\dfrac{3}{\pi}$ times the sum of all possible values of $\alpha$ is
6a7a1ff88d64bc5514693b17.sol:
Let $u = \sin^{-1}x$ and $v = \cos^{-1}y$. Then $u + v = \alpha$.

Taking the sine of both sides:
$\sin(u+v) = \sin\alpha$
$\sin u \cos v + \cos u \sin v = \sin\alpha$

Since $x, y \in (0,1)$, we have $u, v \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.
Thus, $\sin u = x \implies \cos u = \sqrt{1-x^2}$ and $\cos v = y \implies \sin v = \sqrt{1-y^2}$.

Substituting these into the expansion:
$xy + \sqrt{1-x^2}\sqrt{1-y^2} = \sin\alpha$
$\sqrt{1-x^2}\sqrt{1-y^2} = \sin\alpha - xy$

Squaring both sides:
$(1-x^2)(1-y^2) = \sin^2\alpha - 2xy\sin\alpha + x^2y^2$
$1 - x^2 - y^2 + x^2y^2 = \sin^2\alpha - 2xy\sin\alpha + x^2y^2$
$x^2 + y^2 - 2xy\sin\alpha = 1 - \sin^2\alpha = \cos^2\alpha$

Comparing this with the given relation $x^2 + y^2 - \sqrt{3}xy = \dfrac{1}{4}$, we get:
$2\sin\alpha = \sqrt{3} \implies \sin\alpha = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
$\cos^2\alpha = \dfrac{1}{4} \implies \cos\alpha = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$

Since $\alpha \in [0, \pi]$, the possible values for $\alpha$ satisfying both conditions are $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.

The sum of all possible values of $\alpha$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{3} + \dfrac{2\pi}{3} = \pi$.

Multiplying by $\dfrac{3}{\pi}$, we get $\dfrac{3}{\pi} \times \pi = 3$.

Answer: $3$

6a7a1ff8d9da072ecee5832b.sol:
Given $f(x) = \displaystyle \int_{-\sqrt{x}}^{\sqrt{x}} |t| \ln(1+t^2) dt$.

Since the integrand is an even function, we can write:
$f(x) = 2 \displaystyle \int_0^{\sqrt{x}} t \ln(1+t^2) dt$

Let $t^2 = u \Rightarrow 2t dt = du$. The upper limit changes from $\sqrt{x}$ to $x$.
$\Rightarrow f(x) = \displaystyle \int_0^x \ln(1+u) du$

We are also given $g(x) = \displaystyle \int_0^x \dfrac{t}{1+t} dt$.

Adding the two functions:
$f(x) + g(x) = \displaystyle \int_0^x \left( \ln(1+t) + \dfrac{t}{1+t} \right) dt$

Notice that the integrand is the exact derivative of $t \ln(1+t)$.
$\Rightarrow f(x) + g(x) = \left[ t \ln(1+t) \right]_0^x = x \ln(1+x)$

Substitute $x = 3$:
$f(3) + g(3) = 3 \ln(1+3) = 3 \ln 4 = \ln(4^3) = \ln 64$

We need to find the value of $e^{\dfrac{1}{3} (f(3) + g(3))}$:
$e^{\dfrac{1}{3} \ln 64} = e^{\ln(64^{1/3})} = e^{\ln 4} = 4$

Answer: $4$

6a7a1ff8a1f0a8062a4a6c6f.text: Let a region in the first quadrant be bounded by the parabola $y^2 = 6x$ and the line $y = x$. The area of the portion of this region that lies strictly inside the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 16$ is equal to :
6a7a1ff8a1f0a8062a4a6c6f.sol:
The region is bounded by the parabola $y^2 = 6x$ (upper boundary) and the line $y = x$ (lower boundary), and is restricted inside the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 16$.

Find the intersection of the parabola $y^2 = 6x$ and the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 16$ in the first quadrant:
$x^2 + 6x - 16 = 0 \Rightarrow (x+8)(x-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2$

Find the intersection of the line $y = x$ and the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 16$ in the first quadrant:
$x^2 + x^2 = 16 \Rightarrow 2x^2 = 16 \Rightarrow x = 2\sqrt{2}$

The upper boundary of the required region changes at $x = 2$. For $x \in [0, 2]$, the upper boundary is the parabola $y = \sqrt{6x}$. For $x \in [2, 2\sqrt{2}]$, the upper boundary is the circle $y = \sqrt{16-x^2}$. The lower boundary is the line $y = x$ throughout the interval $[0, 2\sqrt{2}]$.

The required area is the sum of two integrals:
$A = \int_0^2 (\sqrt{6x} - x) dx + \int_2^{2\sqrt{2}} (\sqrt{16-x^2} - x) dx$

Evaluate the first integral:
$\int_0^2 (\sqrt{6x} - x) dx = \left[ \dfrac{2\sqrt{6}}{3}x^{3/2} - \dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_0^2 = \dfrac{2\sqrt{6}}{3}(2\sqrt{2}) - 2 = \dfrac{8\sqrt{3}}{3} - 2$

Evaluate the second integral:
$\int_2^{2\sqrt{2}} (\sqrt{16-x^2} - x) dx = \left[ \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{16-x^2} + 8\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{4}\right) - \dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_2^{2\sqrt{2}}$
At $x = 2\sqrt{2}$: $\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{2}\sqrt{8} + 8\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) - \dfrac{8}{2} = 4 + 8\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - 4 = 2\pi$
At $x = 2$: $\dfrac{2}{2}\sqrt{12} + 8\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) - \dfrac{4}{2} = 2\sqrt{3} + 8\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) - 2 = 2\sqrt{3} + \dfrac{4\pi}{3} - 2$
Second integral value $= 2\pi - \left( 2\sqrt{3} + \dfrac{4\pi}{3} - 2 \right) = \dfrac{2\pi}{3} - 2\sqrt{3} + 2$

Total Area $= \left( \dfrac{8\sqrt{3}}{3} - 2 \right) + \left( \dfrac{2\pi}{3} - 2\sqrt{3} + 2 \right) = \dfrac{2\pi}{3} + \dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2\pi}{3} + \dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}$

6a7a1ff8a5f5ebb8fa9e3db2.sol:
Let the circumcentre $O$ be the origin of the reference frame.

The position vectors of the vertices $A$, $B$, and $C$ are $\vec{OA}$, $\vec{OB}$, and $\vec{OC}$ respectively.

We know that the position vector of the orthocentre $H$ relative to the circumcentre $O$ is given by $\vec{OH} = \vec{OA} + \vec{OB} + \vec{OC}$.

The given expression is $\vec{HA} + \vec{HB} + \vec{HC}$.

Using the triangle law of vector addition, we can write $\vec{HA} = \vec{OA} - \vec{OH}$, and similarly for the others.

Thus, $\vec{HA} + \vec{HB} + \vec{HC} = (\vec{OA} - \vec{OH}) + (\vec{OB} - \vec{OH}) + (\vec{OC} - \vec{OH})$

$= (\vec{OA} + \vec{OB} + \vec{OC}) - 3\vec{OH}$

Substituting $\vec{OA} + \vec{OB} + \vec{OC} = \vec{OH}$, we get:

$= \vec{OH} - 3\vec{OH} = -2\vec{OH}$

$= 2\vec{HO}$

Answer: $2\vec{HO}$

6a7a1ff8a63b55a6425df0c7.text: Let $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ be two unit vectors such that the angle between them is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. If $\vec{c}$ is a non-zero vector such that $\vec{a} + 3\vec{b}$ is collinear with $\vec{c}$ and $\vec{b} + 4\vec{c}$ is collinear with $\vec{a}$, then the value of $144|\vec{c}|^2$ is equal to
6a7a1ff8a63b55a6425df0c7.sol:
Given that $\vec{a} + 3\vec{b}$ is collinear with $\vec{c}$, we can write:
$\vec{a} + 3\vec{b} = \lambda \vec{c} \quad \dots (1)$

Also, $\vec{b} + 4\vec{c}$ is collinear with $\vec{a}$, so:
$\vec{b} + 4\vec{c} = \mu \vec{a} \implies \vec{c} = \dfrac{\mu}{4}\vec{a} - \dfrac{1}{4}\vec{b} \quad \dots (2)$

Substituting $(2)$ into $(1)$ gives:
$\vec{a} + 3\vec{b} = \lambda \left( \dfrac{\mu}{4}\vec{a} - \dfrac{1}{4}\vec{b} \right)$

Rearranging the terms, we get:
$\left( 1 - \dfrac{\lambda \mu}{4} \right)\vec{a} + \left( 3 + \dfrac{\lambda}{4} \right)\vec{b} = \vec{0}$

Since $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are non-collinear (the angle between them is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$), their coefficients must be zero:
$3 + \dfrac{\lambda}{4} = 0 \implies \lambda = -12$
$1 - \dfrac{\lambda \mu}{4} = 0 \implies 1 - \dfrac{-12 \mu}{4} = 0 \implies \mu = -\dfrac{1}{3}$

Using $\lambda = -12$ in equation $(1)$, we have:
$\vec{a} + 3\vec{b} = -12\vec{c} \implies \vec{c} = -\dfrac{1}{12}(\vec{a} + 3\vec{b})$

Now, we find $144|\vec{c}|^2$:
$144|\vec{c}|^2 = |\vec{a} + 3\vec{b}|^2 = |\vec{a}|^2 + 9|\vec{b}|^2 + 6(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b})$

Since $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are unit vectors with an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$:
$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = |\vec{a}||\vec{b}|\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = (1)(1)\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Thus,
$144|\vec{c}|^2 = 1 + 9(1) + 6\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 1 + 9 + 3 = 13$.

Answer: $13$
